subject: Ownership split: A/B prompt sets, acceptance thresholds, and escalation path
messages:
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
To: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Tom Morris <tmorris@lumalabs.com>
Date: 2027-04-25T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Ownership split: A/B prompt sets, acceptance thresholds, and escalation path

Hi team —

I ran a quick eval over the weekend (attached) against the two candidate prompt sets for Luma Labs. The high-level ask from their PM is: decide ownership, tie down acceptance criteria for the A/B, and define an escalation/rollback path if we see a quality regression after rollout.

Proposed start point (please critique):
- Promptset A: baseline (current prod phrasing). Owner: Engs on dedicated infra.
- Promptset B: experimental rewrite with new system message and shorter instructions. Owner: Product for prompt tuning + Dev for infra metrics.
- Acceptance criteria: no >2.0 percentage-point drop in correctness on the key 5 intents; macro F1 for intents must not drop >1.5 points; mean latency increase <= 15ms.
- Rollback triggers: if two consecutive daily batches show any metric crossing the acceptance delta above, auto-fallback to Promptset A.
- Escalation: notify product lead -> CS -> Eng oncall; open JIRA SUP if customer-facing degradation >1h.

Questions I need by EOD: who will be the A owner and who takes B? Do the thresholds above look doable for a canary of 1% traffic ramp to 10% over 24 hours?

Attachments: evaluation_report_v0.pdf, ab_sample_metrics.csv

Thanks,
Monica
Monica Patel
Product Manager, Evals
Redwood Inference
From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Tom Morris <tmorris@lumalabs.com>
Date: 2027-04-25T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Ownership split: A/B prompt sets, acceptance thresholds, and escalation path

On Sun, Apr 25, 2027 at 9:12 AM Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com> wrote:
> I ran a quick eval over the weekend (attached) against the two candidate prompt sets for Luma Labs.

Thanks Monica — quick clarifying questions from infra side:
- When you say "two consecutive daily batches", how big is a batch (requests or users)? We should align that to the telemetry windows we already collect (5m, 1h, 24h). I prefer 1h rolling windows for canaries and 24h for final decisions.
- For the latency goal, is that p50 or p95? p95 matters more for UX.

Proposed changes from infra:
- Use p95 latency <= 30ms as the canary threshold (we can do 15ms for p50 if you want).
- Define batch size as 1,000 requests for canary checks or 1% of daily traffic, whichever is larger.

I can own the infra-side will-rollback automation (hook into routing rules) if Monica and Product confirm owners and thresholds.

-Dev
Dev Patel
SRE, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference
From: Tom Morris <tmorris@lumalabs.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-25T11:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Ownership split: A/B prompt sets, acceptance thresholds, and escalation path

Thanks Monica and team — appreciate the clear ask. A couple of quick notes from Luma:
- We run a slightly different intent taxonomy in prod than what's in your report; we'll share a mapping this afternoon. Can you incorporate that before final acceptance gating?
- Timeline: we want a 2-week experiment window but are flexible if your automation and monitoring are set.

We also prefer that counterfactual evals (rerun historical traffic in a dry run) are performed prior to any public rollout. Is that something you can schedule?

Happy to hop on a 30 min sync if useful.

Tom
Tom Morris
Product Lead
Luma Labs
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Tom Morris <tmorris@lumalabs.com>
Date: 2027-04-25T13:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Ownership split: A/B prompt sets, acceptance thresholds, and escalation path

Agree with Dev's infra adjustments. A couple of concrete commitments from me (product/quality):
- I'll take ownership for Promptset B quality tracking and for running the human-in-the-loop checks during canary.
- Acceptance criteria updates: intent macro F1 drop threshold set to 1.0 points (stricter), correctness drop capped at 1.5 percentage points. p95 latency threshold for canary: 30ms.
- We'll run a counterfactual pass on last 14 days of production traffic and produce a short delta report (will attach).

I'll open JIRA SUP-4829 to track automation and escalation hooks. Monica: can you add the Luma intent mapping link when it arrives?

Rishi Malhotra
Product Manager, Model Quality
Redwood Inference
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>, Tom Morris <tmorris@lumalabs.com>
Date: 2027-04-25T17:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Ownership split: A/B prompt sets, acceptance thresholds, and escalation path

Thanks all — quick wrap and decisions:
- Owners: Promptset A owner = Dev (infra rollout/fallback hooks), Promptset B owner = Rishi (quality + human checks).
- Thresholds: correctness <= 1.5pp drop, macro F1 <= 1.0 point drop, p95 latency <= 30ms.
- Canary plan: counterfactual pass (Rishi) by Tue; 1% traffic -> 10% over 24h if no flags (Dev to implement automation); 48h observation window after full 10% ramp before next increase.
- Escalation: any single-hour window exceeding thresholds -> immediate rollback and open JIRA SUP-4829; customer notification via CS; exec notification if customer impact >1h.

Monica: please own the timeline doc + shareability with Luma (and add their intent mapping). Rishi/Dev: sync with each other tomorrow morning to wire checks. Tom: let us know the mapping when possible and we will schedule the counterfactual run.

Laura
Laura Bennett
VP, Product Operations
Redwood Inference
